violated_invariant: Control of the Timelock (and therefore every gov-gated escape hatch such as masterFallback) must not be obtainable by a single ~3% token holder; quorumVotes/proposalThreshold are fixed absolute numbers with no participation floor, so with zero other voters one self-delegated stake clears both.
notes: Every contract behaved as written: the attacker bought ~504K YAM with real capital, self-delegated, and alone cleared the fixed quorum (2e29) and threshold on a dormant DAO, then took Timelock admin and used the gov-only masterFallback on both UMA farming contracts. Labeled governance_design rather than out-of-scope designed behavior because the taxonomy reserves that value for exactly this failure, but a reviewer could reasonably call it designed behavior, hence medium confidence. No Slither detector describes a low-quorum governance capture; the arbitrary-send/arbitrary-from findings are gated or governance-controlled and are false positives.

violated_invariant: Only an authorized caller may route a call through the Router to the Safe module; the Router's authorization check short-circuits to true when the multicall target is the Router itself, so a self-referential multicall runs the nested payload with the Router's own trusted identity.
notes: The defect is in the unverified private DeFi-Saver-style Router (0x4f00) whose multicall(address,bytes[]) trusts target==address(this); the enabled module (0xea18, also unverified) then forwards a DELEGATECALL recipe into the victim Safe. Neither defect contract has recovered source, so the location names come from the PoC/trace, not from Sourcify. The two candidates with source (GnosisSafeProxy, Aave aToken proxy) are forwarding proxies/dependencies, so no Slither finding is adjudicated and none explains the exploit.

violated_invariant: Vault share price must only reflect value the Strategy actually deposited; instead balanceOfY() values a Convex staked balance that anyone can inflate via permissionless stakeFor at the metapool's spot get_virtual_price, so a depositor can raise NAV between deposit and withdraw.
notes: The on-chain Strategy (0xb8d6) is a thin dispatcher: deposited() delegatecalls a governance-set impl (0xFf20DE3f, not among the candidates) that prices BaseRewardPool.balanceOf(Strategy) at spot virtual price; the NAV-inflation logic therefore lives partly outside the recovered source. Slither's controlled-delegatecall findings are false positives (fixed selector, impl set by governance) and no detector describes manipulable NAV accounting.

violated_invariant: initializeAccount must be callable at most once per account; the only guard is a transient-storage flag set in AccountProxy's constructor, which EIP-1153 keeps alive for the whole transaction, so anyone in the same tx can re-initialize a freshly deployed, pre-funded account with a malicious bootstrap.
notes: AccountProxy.sol and Initializable.sol (tstore/tload INIT_SLOT) are in the factory's recovered source and confirm the PoC; the account implementation 0x000000b8 that exposes initializeAccount is not a candidate, so that location is named from the PoC. Slither has no detector for transient-storage scoping, and its findings on the factory are generic (msg.value reachability, unused returns in OZ ERC1967Utils, benign reentrancy).

violated_invariant: UController.newOrganization must not register a caller-supplied avatar as a full-permission scheme over a Reputation contract that already belongs to another organization; it trusts the avatar's own nativeReputation() answer and never checks prior registration.
notes: The defect contract (shared UController 0xd5be) and the Avatar/Reputation/SchemeRegistrar are all unverified; only the unrelated DAOToken (GDT) has recovered source, so locations are named from the PoC's trace-decoded selectors. Attacker minted 20,000 REP against the real Reputation, voted itself in as a 0x1F scheme and drained 4.025 ETH. No Slither finding bears on the causal code.

violated_invariant: Total ETH paid back to a depositor (immediate bonus refund plus later withdraw) must not exceed the ETH deposited; deposit() both refunds the first-deposit bonus in ETH and adds the same bonus to the user's redeemable MUS allocation, with no cap.
notes: Sourcify has a partial match for MUSystem.sol even though the PoC calls the victim unverified; deposit() computes d.bonus, adds it to userTokenObtain and separately refunds amtToSend, which withdraw() never nets against. The attacker cycled fresh addresses with its own WETH (the PoC's flash loan is only working capital), so mechanism is 'other'. Slither's incorrect-equality on boolean compares and the arbitrary-send-eth on the owner fee transfer are false positives.

violated_invariant: A Safe module may only act for the Safe that actually enabled it, and may only call vetted routers; _start authenticates by asking msg.sender whether the module is enabled (self-attestation) and _swap does router.call(data) with caller-supplied router and data, so a fake Safe can make the adapter call execTransactionFromModule on real Safes that enabled it.
notes: Both flaws are confirmed in the verified adapter source (lines 92 and 189). Finding 1 (low-level-calls) points at the exact router.call(data) site but the detector only flags use of a low-level call, not an attacker-controlled target, so it is not counted as explaining. The Aave pool and Morpho candidates are infrastructure, not victims.

violated_invariant: Each unit of ETH received must be added to totalRewards exactly once; claimRewards adds (balance - lastETHBalance) on every call but only refreshes lastETHBalance when claimable > 0, so claimRewards([]) re-counts the same donation delta without bound.
notes: Verified source lines 1407-1432 match the PoC exactly. Slither flags claimRewards only for an uninitialized local (claimable, intentionally zero) and a low-level ETH send; neither describes the accounting asymmetry. The flash loan only supplied the ~27 ETH donation and was repaid.

violated_invariant: Expired buy-windows must settle at a manipulation-resistant price and only by an entitled party; accept() is open to anyone once expiry passes and _closeWindow/_buyBack use the same pool's instantaneous getSlot0 price with sqrtPriceLimit at MIN_SQRT_PRICE+1, so escrowed ETH can be mispositioned around a flash-moved spot and swept.
notes: All three facts (ungated accept after expiry at line 287, spot-price backInPlace test at 386, unbounded _buyBack limit at 443) are in the full-match source. Slither's 'timestamp' on accept() and 'unused-return' on getSlot0/swap touch the causal functions but describe different weaknesses, so explains is empty. The lib/v4-core findings (FullMath, BitMath, Hooks) are dependency code and were not adjudicated.

violated_invariant: Interest for an idle period must be accrued once at the utilization that prevailed during it; _checkFirstAction stores the whole 264,059-block gap and freezes actionEXR for the block, and the interest model then multiplies that full gap by a rate recomputed from live totals on every later action in the same block, so a flash-loan depositor sets the rate and collects ~36 days of interest repeatedly.
notes: The handler logic (TokenHandler, partial match) confirms _checkFirstAction; the interest model 0x29ec that applies the stored gap is not among the candidates, so that location is named from the PoC. UsdtHandlerProxy is a forwarding proxy and the affected market, not the defect. Slither's unused-return findings 70/85 sit on _checkFirstAction but only complain about ignored booleans, so they do not explain the exploit.
